subtopic: Gradient Boosted Decision Trees (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost)
question_text: [Supervised & Unsupervised Modeling - Q33] How does gradient boosting differ fundamentally from random forest bagging?

options.text: Random forests build trees sequentially to minimize residual errors, while gradient boosting builds independent trees in parallel
Gradient boosting fits subsequent trees to the negative gradients (pseudo-residuals) of the loss function, whereas bagging aggregates independent bootstrapped trees
Gradient boosting can only solve binary classification problems
Random forest bagging requires learning rate hyperparameter tuning

answer_explanation: Bagging reduces variance by averaging decorrelated independent models. Boosting reduces bias by iteratively adding weak learners that fit the residuals of prior ensembles.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: Bagging reduces variance by averaging decorrelated independent models. Boosting reduces bias by iteratively adding weak learners that fit the residuals of prior ensembles.
